location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 success; cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock
issue: The CAP-7 success test (both browser:<engine> phases start before either ends) is satisfied even when the lock fully serializes the engines, because lock-wait time sits inside the browser phase. On bankwire, the universal smoke and 4 of the 5 authored specs have a BO goto, so they take the lock exclusive. checkout-with-bank holds it through about 38 FO checkout steps. Only checkout-empty-banks-safe can overlap. 'Boots once' is also already today's behavior (brownfield: one boot per version, engines run sequentially). So CAP-7 can pass its test while delivering about zero concurrency, plus added snapshot-db cost and rerun-seq risk.
implementation_impact: The implementer builds worker subprocesses, locks, snapshots and sequential confirmation passes, and the test cannot tell whether any time was saved. The before/after report can show browser time unchanged or worse while CAP-7 counts as done.
suggestion: Replace the overlap assertion with a measured one: on bankwire, the union of browser:<engine> intervals minus total lock-wait must be shorter than the sum of the single-engine browser phases from the baseline, or report the achieved overlap ratio in the timing report. State in CAP-7 the expected gain for BO-heavy modules, and say whether per-scenario lock granularity is accepted knowing it serializes nearly all of bankwire.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock and Parallel-only failures; Scenario prerequisites (bankwire requires)
issue: The lock stops scenarios from overlapping but does not control order across engines, and global shop state persists after a BO scenario ends. Engine A can finish checkout-with-bank (it adds the global bank account 'Bank Niaga E2E') before engine B starts checkout-empty-banks-safe. B then exercises the configured-banks path, not the empty-banks path. A module bug in the empty-banks path is caught on A and silently missed on B: B has no findings, so no rerun-seq runs. That is a false pass for (V, B), which breaks the honesty law. The identical-findings test only injects the step-55 fault, which every interleaving catches, so it cannot detect this class.
implementation_impact: Parallel mode can make a cell pass gate-grade with coverage that differs from a sequential run. The 'findings identical to one cold single-engine run per engine' claim holds only for faults that do not depend on order.
suggestion: Add a cross-engine ordering barrier: no engine starts the scenario at run-order index k+1 until every engine has finished index k (engines run the same topological list). Alternatively, any scenario that mutates global state (BO) acts as a barrier for later scenarios on all engines. Add a live fixture whose fault appears only in the empty-banks path, and assert both engines report it in parallel mode.

location: tier-matrix.md > Rules (Tier 1 runs in Phase 2 ... Layer 3 lenses spawn at the start of Phase 2 as today); references/run-phases.md > Fase 2
issue: Tier 1, the multi-hour cold release gate, starts in parallel with the Layer 3 adversarial lenses. Layer 3 takes minutes and often demands a source patch. Any blocking Layer 3 finding that is fixed stales every E2E cell (source_fingerprint), so the whole tier 1 run, and then the canary, must be redone. This is the most expensive kind of wasted work, and the spec exists to cut wall-clock.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator wastes a full tier 1 (2-3 boots × both browsers) whenever Layer 3 or the cross-version static scan finds something worth patching. The bankwire before/after report will not show this cost because it measures a clean module.
suggestion: Make tier 1 wait until the current Phase 2 Layer 3 merge has no blocking finding (or Layer 3 is reused). Equivalently, add 'Layer 3 merged and clean' to the Phase 2 entry/tier 1 start condition, and spawn lenses at the end of Phase 1 when every version is clean on Layers 1, 2 and 5 and the canary is gate-ready.

issue: Within one cell's history, 'newest' is the highest started_at (wall-clock, written by different processes), with ties broken by run_id (random hex). WSL2 is known for clock jumps after host sleep or hibernate, and the append-only history already has a monotonic per-cell order (line position under LOCK_EX) that the spec ignores. A clock step backwards can rank an older passing gate-grade record above a newer gate-grade fail, so 'a newer gate-grade fail always overrides an older pass' no longer holds and ready can become true wrongly.
implementation_impact: Plan, aggregate and the failed-only selection can pick the wrong record after a clock adjustment, with no error shown, in the direction that breaks the honesty law.
suggestion: Order records of one cell by append position (line order), which the locked appends already make total. Use started_at only for cross-cell questions (newest run for the focus cell), and treat a record whose started_at is earlier than the previous line's as a clock anomaly to log. Add a test that appends a fail with an earlier started_at after a pass and expects ready=false.

issue: The fingerprint covers every file under the module, with only .git/, top-level .psm-*, .memlog.md and the reports dir excluded, and ss.is_skipped is explicitly not used. It therefore covers editor swap and backup files (.*.swp, *~, #*#), __pycache__/*.pyc, .idea/, .vscode/, .DS_Store, and node_modules churn. Opening any module file in vim during a multi-hour tier 1 run creates and later deletes a swap file, so every record of that run goes stale and the whole gate repeats.
implementation_impact: Spurious full re-proofs that cost hours each and look to the operator like 'evidence went stale for no reason'. The dominant wait the spec is meant to remove comes back through a side channel.
suggestion: Define a small, explicit, tested ignore list of editor and OS temp patterns (swap/backup files, .DS_Store, __pycache__, IDE dirs) that PrestaShop never loads, kept in the shared source_fingerprint function and newest_source_mtime. Add a test: creating and deleting a .x.php.swp file leaves every cell fresh. Alternatively, warn in the run output when the fingerprint changed during a run and name the files that changed.

issue: The pain is 'roughly a full day per validation', but the report never measures a validation session end to end. The fix-loop 'after' slice is one warm iteration: it leaves out the keeper boot and baseline dump (charged to the iteration that started the keeper), the mandatory cold-canary promotion run that must follow it, and Firefox (the 'before' iteration drives both browsers). The gate slice runs on an already-clean module, so loop-backs and the cost of the first failing canary run are never seen. The report can show a large speedup while a real session gets slower.
implementation_impact: The 'numeric wall-clock target set later from it' will be calibrated on slices that favor the new design. Regressions such as warm/cold alternation or rerun-seq overhead would not show.
suggestion: Add one end-to-end measurement per side: starting from the injected fault, one patch reverts it, then the run goes until the plan reports done (after) or the old flow's ready (before), timed around the whole session. Record keeper_boot and the cold-canary promotion in the fix-loop slice, and state that Firefox in the fix loop is deferred, not removed.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan step 7 (diverges) and Warm container > Teardown
issue: Divergence (a warm or partial pass newer than a cold full fail) is checked only on the current fingerprint, so the knowledge that the warm container masks this bug is lost at every patch. A bug the warm reset cannot reproduce (for example a modified pre-existing file, which is explicitly not restored) gives this cycle on every patch: warm iteration passes, then the cold-version or cold-canary promotion fails, then the next derivation is warm again. Each cold promotion also tears down the keeper (Teardown: keepers are stopped before any run without --warm), so the next warm iteration pays pull, bring-up, wait-healthy and baseline again. The fix loop becomes slower than cold-only, and nothing in the plan detects it.
implementation_impact: In exactly the residue cases the spec admits the warm reset misses, the operator gets misleading green warm results and double boot cost per iteration, with no automatic fallback.
suggestion: Record a session-scoped 'warm-contradicted' flag per cell: once a cold full fail follows a warm pass for that cell in the current --session (any fingerprint), e2e_warm stays false for the rest of the session, as it already does for warm-reset and keeper-start. Add a plan test for warm pass, then cold fail, then patch, which derives a cold focus run.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage; Headless (config copy); tier-matrix.md > Visual review (visual-pending)
issue: Cell histories are append-only with no retention or compaction. Each record carries findings, screenshots, scenario_spans, phase timings and notes, and every plan, aggregate and ps-run-layer call reads and parses every line of every configured cell. Headless also writes a new <module>-psm-config.headless.<session>.json for every call and never deletes it. Over months of fix loops this grows without bound, and a corrupt tail line (the corrupt-history rule) can only be cleared by a new valid run.
implementation_impact: Plan latency and report-dir clutter grow over time. No rule says whether manually pruning a history file is allowed or how pruning interacts with 'newest gate-grade' and the blocked-infra two-newest rule.
suggestion: Specify a retention rule. For example: ps-run-layer compacts a history under LOCK_EX when it exceeds N lines, keeping the newest record of each (fingerprint, boot, scenario_set) plus the last K records. Also specify that headless deletes its config copy before returning (or reuses one per module).

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > session; Warm container > Owner / Chain
issue: The session token, which is the warm owner token, exists only in the orchestrator's (LLM) context and is minted again on every psm-validate invocation. Context compaction, a crash, or simply re-invoking psm-validate to continue the fix loop gives a new token. The previous keeper then becomes 'another owner': it is never reused or stopped, holds a psm_e2e_slots slot for up to the 60-minute TTL, needs Budi's OK to stop, and a second keeper for the same (module, version) boots. blocked-infra and the warm-reset/keeper-start memory also reset without anyone noticing.
implementation_impact: Fix-loop restarts, which are common in interactive use, leak warm containers and slots and double the warm boot cost. Repeated identical infra failures can loop across invocations without ever reaching blocked-infra.
suggestion: Persist the session token per module in the reports dir (for example <module>-psm-session with creation time). On Activation, offer to resume it when it is younger than the warm TTL. Or, at minimum, let ps-run-layer adopt this module's keeper when its owner token's session file says the session is resumed.

location: cell-contract.md > Scenario prerequisites (requires) — duplicate-name and validation rules; Docs to update
issue: The new validation in discover_scenarios skips specs that share an effective name, that are named psm-universal-smoke, or that have bad requires. Today such specs run. For any existing module with duplicate spec names (common after copy-paste, since the name falls back to the file stem only when absent), those specs now drop out with a scenario note, so a module that was ready becomes not ready right after the upgrade. Neither brownfield.md nor 'Docs to update' mentions this breaking change or a migration check, and e2e-quickstart is only told about requires.
implementation_impact: Other modules in the repo can fail validation at the first run after the upgrade for a reason unrelated to their code, and the operator only finds out after a gate run.
suggestion: Add to brownfield/Docs to update: a one-time scan of all modules/*/tests/e2e/*.json for duplicate effective names and reserved names, run as part of the implementation (fix the fixtures or document them), and a quickstart note that spec names must be unique per module.

location: cell-contract.md > Scenario prerequisites — bankwire requires list
issue: checkout-with-bank declares bankwire-checkout-empty-banks-safe in requires, but that spec is not a prerequisite. It does not set up any state checkout-with-bank needs, it only has to run before banks exist. requires is defined as a prerequisite relation that drives failed-only selection and topological order. Using it to mean 'must run before' blurs the meaning the fixture is supposed to demonstrate, and it adds an unrelated scenario to every failed-only rerun of checkout-with-bank (with the fault, the rerun is 5 of 6 scenarios, so CAP-4 saves almost nothing on its own reference fixture).
implementation_impact: Module authors copying the fixture learn to list ordering dependencies as prerequisites. The CAP-4 benefit shown on bankwire is close to zero, which weakens the before/after evidence for failed-only reruns.
suggestion: Either drop checkout-empty-banks-safe from checkout-with-bank's requires (file-name order already puts it first), or state in the spec that requires also expresses 'must run before'. Then document the cost/benefit honestly: the failed-only gain depends on how deep the requires chain is.

location: SPEC.md > CAP-3; cell-contract.md > Runner > Fail-fast; Config keys > psm_e2e_slots
issue: With the default psm_e2e_slots=6 and the default 3×2 matrix, tier 1 needs cost 2 + 2 (two non-canary versions, both browsers in parallel) + 1 (canary version, Firefox) = 5 slots. So every tier-1 cell is admitted at once, and fail-fast never prevents a single boot in the default configuration. CAP-3 is only exercised under the stubbed --slots 1 test or host contention. The spec presents fail-fast as a time saver but does not admit that it is inert by default.
implementation_impact: The implementer builds queueing, cancellation of wait-slots and not-run records that cost complexity but give no benefit on the target host unless other sessions occupy slots.
suggestion: Decide explicitly. Either accept CAP-3 as a contention-only safeguard and say so in CAP-3. Or order tier 1 admission so fail-fast can bite (for example, admit the oldest non-canary version first and the others only after its browsers pass), and measure the trade-off in the timing report.

location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade > Fresh; Warm container > Pre-iteration check
issue: Freshness and the warm pre-iteration check compare the image tag string only. A re-pulled image under the same tag (rolling flashlight tags such as 9.1 pick up new PrestaShop patch releases), or a locally rebuilt image, leaves every old record 'fresh' and the warm container 'matching', so evidence from a different PrestaShop build counts as gate-grade.
implementation_impact: ready can be true on evidence gathered against a core build that is no longer the one the module targets, without any staleness reason being reported.
suggestion: Record the resolved image ID (docker image inspect --format {{.Id}}) next to image_tag in each record and in session.json, and make freshness require both the tag and the ID to match the current local image. Report a new stale reason, stale-image, when only the ID differs.
